$$

$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,3,1)$ and is parallel to the vector ![](images/80/80cf9513aeb2ab2f87dda54ca16cdab76ff55024be1f7822fc9d1434b62382de.svg)" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186124230 :question/worked-solution "First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. $$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 9t \\ -7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-t \\ -5+9t \\ 3-7t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t \in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

point $P(3,-1,7)$ and that's parallel to the direction vector ![](images/54/54405c5c6e2502e5174525c2ee36a99366a79933b47e316a09858f827fda8dae.svg) As we know, we can write the vector equation of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Using the vector equation above, we can create a set of **parametric equations** where we express a general point $(x,y,z)$ in terms of  the parameter $t.$

If we let ![](images/67/67b8360f90540ffb75d39717c375f0ef6e9a8a39cae5832c78957105e0d148b6.svg) be the position vector of the general point $(x,y,z),$ then the above equation can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1+5t \\ 7-3t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:
![](images/64/64cf325014eff341673557321ef565e35988b836630f3fbeb52af8024d7aaad7.svg)

The equations in the above system are called the **parametric equations** of the straight line.
Geometrically, the equation states that a point belongs to the line if and only if its coordinates have the form

$$
(3, \: -1+5t, \: 7-3t),
$$

where $t \in (-\infty, \infty).$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=3 \\ y=-1+5t \\ z=7-3t\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

where $t \in (-\infty, \infty).$
